nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers. If $n$ is $k$-rough and $n$ is positive with every prime factor less than $k + 1$, then $n = 1$.
nodes.title: Only $1$ is rough and smooth at the same bound

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $p$ and $k$ with $p$ prime, $p$ is $k$-rough if and only if $k < p$.
nodes.title: A prime is rough exactly above the bound

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, $n$ is $k$-rough if and only if $n \neq 0$ and every prime in the list of prime factors of $n$ (with multiplicity) is greater than $k$.
nodes.title: Roughness through the list of prime factors

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, $n$ is $k$-rough if and only if $n \neq 0$ and every prime $p$ dividing $n$ satisfies $k < p$.
nodes.title: Characterization of rough numbers

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$, $n$ and $k$, the product $mn$ is $k$-rough if and only if both $m$ and $n$ are $k$-rough.
nodes.title: A product is rough exactly when both factors are

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k$, the number $1$ is $k$-rough.
nodes.title: The number $1$ is rough

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers. Then $n$ is $k$-rough if $n \neq 0$ and every prime $p$ dividing $n$ satisfies $k < p$; that is, $n$ is positive and has no prime factor at most $k$.
nodes.title: Rough numbers

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $k$ and $p$ be natural numbers. If $n$ is $k$-rough and $p$ is a prime dividing $n$, then $k < p$.
nodes.title: Prime divisors of a rough number exceed the bound

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $N$ and $k$ be natural numbers. If $n$ is $k$-rough, $n \le N$ and $n \ne 1$, then $n$ belongs to the set of natural numbers $m$ with $1 \le m \le N$ that are not $(k+1)$-smooth, where $m$ is $(k+1)$-smooth when $m > 0$ and every prime factor of $m$ is less than $k + 1$; for $m \ge 1$, not being $(k+1)$-smooth means having a prime factor $p \ge k + 1$.
nodes.title: Rough numbers other than $1$ lie in Mathlib's rough numbers up to a bound

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$, $n$ and $k$, if $m$ and $n$ are both $k$-rough, then $mn$ is $k$-rough.
nodes.title: Products of rough numbers are rough

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k$, every $k$-rough natural number $n$ satisfies $n \ne 0$.
nodes.title: Rough numbers are nonzero

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number. If a natural number $m$ is $k$-rough and $d$ is a nonzero divisor of $m$, then $d$ is $k$-rough.
nodes.title: Divisors of rough numbers are rough

nodes.summary: Let $k$ and $l$ be natural numbers with $l \le k$. Every $k$-rough natural number is $l$-rough.
nodes.title: Roughness is antitone in the bound

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k$, every $k$-rough natural number $n$ satisfies $n > 0$.
nodes.title: Rough numbers are positive

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
